Ui.Script:
NUM_SHAPESHIFT_SLOTS = 10
-- RIGHT-CLICK IS DEAD HERE, and deliberately (decision 1030 reverting 1027). The ref's -- ShapeshiftButtonTemplate registers NOTHING: it inherits ActionButtonTemplate and then -- overrides <OnLoad> with a body that only scales the cooldown, so the -- `RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp","RightButtonUp")` that ActionButton_OnLoad gives every -- other action-style button (ref ActionButton.lua:109) is lost and the default -- {LeftButtonUp} stands. A right-press therefore neither flashes the pushed art -- (0x77924b gates that on the same mask) nor casts. It reads like a Blizzard oversight -- and it is the only bar that behaves this way — reproduced anyway, because the director -- checked it against the reference and called faithful. function BenillaShapeshiftButton_OnLoad(button, index) button.index = index button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") end
-- The CheckButton widget toggles itself BEFORE OnClick fires (the widget contract); the -- ref immediately reverts that toggle (ShapeshiftButtonTemplate OnClick, ref- -- BonusActionBarFrame.xml l.31-38), so the checked ring never follows the click — only -- the isActive repaint. That is what keeps a warrior's ACTIVE stance lit through the -- click's silent wire no-op (stances never cancel — the 0x4b4963 guard), and a druid -- form/Stealth lit until the server actually confirms the shift-out. The revert is -- unconditional, which is why no click here can leave a lit form dark — unlike the pet -- bar's flat SetChecked(0), which needs a repaint to be correct. function BenillaShapeshiftButton_OnClick(button) if button:GetChecked() then button:SetChecked(nil) else button:SetChecked(1) end CastShapeshiftForm(button.index) end
-- Hover: the form's spell tooltip through the engine channel (ref ShapeshiftBar's -- GameTooltip:SetShapeshift; decision 0274 P2). Anchor: the ref's ShapeshiftButton -- OnEnter (BonusActionBarFrame.xml l.40-45) takes the default corner when UberTooltips -- is "1" — its byte-verified stock default — and sits beside the button otherwise. Like -- the action bar's, that fork was collapsed to the "1" leg until B230 registered the CVar -- (cvars.rs carries the byte-read); the stock look is unchanged, the off leg is reachable. function BenillaShapeshiftButton_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets if GetCVar("UberTooltips") == "0" then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") else GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, button) end GameTooltip:SetShapeshift(button.index) end
function BenillaShapeshiftButton_OnLeave(button) GameTooltip:Hide() end
-- Ref ShapeshiftBar_Update + ShapeshiftBar_UpdateState fused (SCOPE note above): size the -- bar to the form count (hide the whole frame at 0 — a formless class never shows it), -- then paint each button — icon, checked (active), the 1.0/0.4 castable tint (ref l.210-214), -- cooldown swipe (CooldownFrame_SetTimer, Cooldown.xml's shared transcription). function ShapeshiftBar_Update() local numForms = GetNumShapeshiftForms() if numForms > 0 then -- ── The shelf's LENGTH is the form count (ref l.161-175) ───────────────────── -- The three strips are DECLARED as the >2-form chain (Left → Middle → Right), so -- the one- and two-form shelves have to re-point the end cap. Hiding the middle -- strip does NOT close its gap — a hidden region still resolves its rect, here -- and in the reference — so without this the 42x50 right cap sits 38px past the -- last button as a stray empty recess: a rogue's Stealth with a second, always- -- empty slot beside it. One form pulls the cap back INSIDE the left cap (+12, a -- 54px shelf around the single button); two butt the caps together; past two the -- middle strip carries one slot per extra form and the cap chains off it. if numForms == 1 then ShapeshiftBarRight:SetPoint("LEFT", ShapeshiftBarLeft, "LEFT", 12, 0) elseif numForms == 2 then ShapeshiftBarRight:SetPoint("LEFT", ShapeshiftBarLeft, "RIGHT", 0, 0) else ShapeshiftBarMiddle:SetPoint("LEFT", ShapeshiftBarLeft, "RIGHT", 0, 0) ShapeshiftBarMiddle:SetWidth(38 * (numForms - 2)) ShapeshiftBarMiddle:SetTexCoord(0, numForms - 2, 0, 1) ShapeshiftBarRight:SetPoint("LEFT", ShapeshiftBarMiddle, "RIGHT", 0, 0) end ShapeshiftBarFrame:Show() else ShapeshiftBarFrame:Hide() end for i = 1, NUM_SHAPESHIFT_SLOTS do local button = getglobal("ShapeshiftButton" .. i) if i <= numForms then local texture, name, isActive, isCastable = GetShapeshiftFormInfo(i) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) local start, duration, enable = GetShapeshiftFormCooldown(i) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(button.cooldown, start, duration, enable) if isActive then button:SetChecked(1) else button:SetChecked(0) end if isCastable then button.icon:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) else button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) end button:Show() else button:Hide() end end -- The art depends on the form COUNT too (the middle strip's `> 2`), so it is re-derived -- here as well as on every managed-position pass. Pure derivation, so running it twice -- costs nothing and missing it costs a strip. ShapeshiftBar_UpdatePosition() end
-- ── The raised/unraised ART fork (ref ShapeshiftBar_UpdatePosition, l.229-251) ────────── -- The reference's function does TWO things and we only owe it one. Its two SetPoints — -- MainMenuBar TOPLEFT +(30,45) with the bottom-left multibar up, +(30,0) without — are -- already `UIParent_ManageFramePositions`' job here: `ShapeshiftBarFrame` is a managed row -- (baseY 0, bottomLeft 45, xOffset 30), which IS those two positions, and a second -- SetPoint from this file would be a competing answer to a question already answered. -- What the pass does NOT carry is the art half, and that is this: -- -- raised — the three shelf strips hidden, each button's ring 50x50. The shelf art IS -- the bar's border and only reads as one while the bar sits on the main bar; -- a row up it would draw across whatever is underneath (the same rule the -- pass applies to the pet bar's sliding strips). -- unraised — the two END-CAPS shown, the MIDDLE strip shown only past two forms, each -- button's ring 64x64. -- -- The `> 2` on the middle strip is the ref's own and easy to miss: a two-form class (a -- priest with Shadowform, a warrior before Berserker) gets the end caps and no middle. -- -- **This became load-bearing with 1500.** While the bottom bars were always on (0270) the -- raised branch was the only reachable state and this whole fork was dead code; now every -- form class sees the UNRAISED bar on a fresh character, so the shelf-less version would be -- the shipped default look rather than an edge case. -- -- It keeps the reference's NAME because the corpus replaces that name wholesale: -- CT_BottomBar.lua:712/741 saves and overwrites `ShapeshiftBar_UpdatePosition` to take the -- bar over. The listener below therefore calls it through the GLOBAL, so an addon that -- replaces it really does take the art with it. function ShapeshiftBar_UpdatePosition() local raised = MultiBarBottomLeft and MultiBarBottomLeft:IsShown() local ring = 64 if raised then ring = 50 ShapeshiftBarLeft:Hide() ShapeshiftBarMiddle:Hide() ShapeshiftBarRight:Hide() else ShapeshiftBarLeft:Show() ShapeshiftBarRight:Show() if GetNumShapeshiftForms() > 2 then ShapeshiftBarMiddle:Show() else ShapeshiftBarMiddle:Hide() end end -- The ref sizes only the buttons a form occupies; ours sizes all ten. Same pixels (a -- hidden button draws nothing) and one less thing to get wrong — a button that appears -- later is already the right size, without this needing to run again for it. for i = 1, NUM_SHAPESHIFT_SLOTS do local ringTexture = getglobal("ShapeshiftButton" .. i .. "NormalTexture") ringTexture:SetWidth(ring) ringTexture:SetHeight(ring) end end
function ShapeshiftBar_OnLoad() local frame = this frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_SHAPESHIFT_FORMS") ShapeshiftBar_Update() end
function ShapeshiftBar_OnEvent() local frame = this ShapeshiftBar_Update() end
-- Re-derive the art after every managed-position recompute (decision 1499's hook — the same -- after-the-pass seam the bag stack registers on). The pass is what decides whether this bar -- is raised, so the art fork has to run when the pass has finished and not before. Called -- through the global name so an addon replacement is honoured (see the function's comment). -- Guarded for the harnesses that load this file without UIParent.xml, the way BagFrame.xml -- guards its own registration. if UIParent_RegisterManagedPositionListener then UIParent_RegisterManagedPositionListener(function() ShapeshiftBar_UpdatePosition() end) end
